slides.title: 1Password got breached via GitHub
slides.body: 1Password shared details of a security incident on Nov 25, 2026. Here is what devs should learn.

slides.title: One employee GitHub account
slides.body: An attacker got into an employee's corporate GitHub account, copied private source code and reached the CI/CD system.
points: Some user names and emails were downloaded

slides.title: Malicious code pushed to backend
slides.body: 1Password says the attacker pushed code to backend services to pull admin data. It restored clean versions and rotated credentials.

slides.title: Your repo is the front door
slides.body: Access to one developer account opened source code and the build pipeline.
points: Protect GitHub like your bank login

slides.title: Lock down your GitHub
points: Never commit secrets; use env variables

slides.title: Is 2FA on your GitHub right now?
slides.body: Reply YES or NOT YET. Be honest.

review.name: Ganesh Sawant
review.text: The team was very professional, supportive, and helpful throughout the entire project. They explained everything clearly.
